newsitem.title: USA: Clinton twists knee after late-night chat.
newsitem.headline: Clinton twists knee after late-night chat.

text.p: President Bill Clinton was taken to hospital early on Friday after twisting his right knee painfully on some steps in the middle of the night but the injury was not serious, the White House said.
"He's fine, he wasn't sedated at all," spokeswoman Mary Ellen Glynn told reporters in Florida. "It looks like the president will not be playing golf today."
Clinton, 50, was taken to St Mary's hospital in West Palm Beach where doctors said the knee had been x-rayed but there were no broken bones.
He was likely to return to Washington later on Friday, a day ahead of schedule.
"He is resting comfortably, he was in some pain," Glynn said.
The accident happened at 1.20 a.m. (0620 GMT) at "Tranquility", the luxurious Florida estate of Australian golfer Greg Norman in Hobe Sound, where the president was staying.
Clinton slipped on some steps while walking to his guest cottage on the estate after staying up late chatting with Norman following a political fund-raising dinner in the state.
Clinton was in Florida to take part in a two-day gold tourney hosted by Norman beginning on Friday.

Since his reelection last November, Clinton and his fellow Democrats have been caught in a swirl of controversy over fund-raising tactics and suggestions that some of the donations bought access to lobby the president or his staff.,
Glynn said there had been no transfer of power to Vice-President Al Gore, as would have happened if Clinton had been rendered incapable of governing.
Clinton is due to meet Russian President Boris Yeltsin in Helsinki next week for talks on NATO expansion into eastern Europe and other matters.
Apart from x-rays, Clinton was also undergoing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to test for torn muscles, the doctors said.
He was seen by his personal physician, U.S. Navy Captain Connie Mariano, who always travels with him.
